title: Broken flagstone road
subject: Subject: an old road of big worn flagstones crossing a moor, about 3 m across. Large flat grey stones, roughly square, many cracked or broken at the corners, with brown trodden earth, grit and white frost in the wide gaps between them, and a few small gaps where a stone is missing. Night, cold blue moonlight, painted with even light.
use: The old road across the cold moor (and a good match for other broken paved roads in the northern wilds).

title: Frozen earth path
subject: Subject: a trodden earth footpath on a cold moor, about 2 m across. Hard frozen brown earth scattered with many small grey and white angular stones and grit, a few faint frost patches. Night, cold blue moonlight, painted with even light.
use: The footpaths on the cold moor and the earth floor of the ruined hut.

title: Frosted moor heather
subject: Subject: open moorland ground seen from above, about 4 m across. A thick low carpet of purple heather mixed with dark blue-green low shrubs, their tips speckled white with frost, a few sprigs of rust-brown dead bracken, small gaps of dark earth. Night, cold blue moonlight, painted with even light.
use: The moor ground between the paths, the rocks and the trees on the cold moor.

title: Dead bracken and heather
subject: Subject: moor ground thick with dead bracken, seen from above, about 3 m across. Curling rust-brown and copper bracken fronds over dark purple heather and dark low shrubs with a few frost-white tips. Night, cold blue moonlight, painted with even light.
use: Patches of the cold moor between the heather, and round the hut and the rise.

title: Ruined hut wall, from the front
subject: Subject: the front wall of a small ruined shepherd's hut on a moor, seen flat from the front. Roughly squared grey stone blocks with moss and lichen, the top edge broken and stepped where stones have fallen, a dark doorway gap and a small window gap, no roof. About 5 m long and 2 m high at its highest. The whole wall is in the picture.
use: The walls of the ruined shepherd's hut on the cold moor.

title: Moor cairn
subject: Subject: a cairn on a moor, seen flat from the side. Rounded and flat grey stones stacked without mortar into a rough cone about 1.2 m tall, the biggest at the bottom, mossy and frosted on top. The whole cairn is in the picture, foot at the bottom.
use: The three cairns that mark the way on the cold moor.

title: Purple heather clump
subject: Subject: one low clump of heather about 40 cm tall, seen from the side: wiry dark stems covered in tiny purple-violet flower spikes, frost on the tips. Whole and alone, with its base at the bottom.
use: Heather clumps scattered on the cold moor and in the undergrowth of the northern camp.

title: Dead bracken clump
subject: Subject: one clump of dead bracken about 80 cm tall, seen from the side: curling copper and rust-brown fronds on thin stems, some bent over, a little frost on the edges. Whole and alone, with its base at the bottom.
use: The dead bracken all over the cold moor.

title: Pale moor grass tussock
subject: Subject: one tussock of dry moor grass about 50 cm tall, seen from the side: thin straw-pale and grey-green blades rising from a tight base and arching outwards, frosted at the tips. Whole and alone, with its base at the bottom.
use: Grass tussocks on the cold moor and round the tarn.

title: Bare frosted twig shrub
subject: Subject: one small leafless shrub about 70 cm tall, seen from the side: thin pale grey twigs fanning up from the base, white with frost. Whole and alone, with its base at the bottom.
use: Bare shrubs on the cold moor.

title: Reeds frozen in ice
subject: Subject: one clump of reeds about 1 m tall, seen from the side, standing up out of ice: thin dark grey-green and straw-coloured blades, straight and bent, with frost along them. Whole and alone, with its base at the bottom.
use: The reed clumps standing in the frozen tarn on the cold moor.
